**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2026. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub mark in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH paper are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

questions.enonce_markdown:
7. (a) Name the following:

(i) **ONE** area covered by the tropical rainforest,
(ii) **ONE** river that flows in the Atlantic basin,
(iii) The Capital of the north region,
(iv) A man-made lake,
(v) A game reserve,
(vi) A dam recently constructed.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
One mark for each correct name (the first example of each row is enough).

| Item | Answer (examples) |
|---|---|
| (i) Area covered by tropical rainforest | **The South Region** (or the East Region, the Littoral, the South-West: for example the Dja Biosphere Reserve, Korup National Park) |
| (ii) River flowing in the Atlantic basin | **The Sanaga** (others: the Wouri, the Nyong, the Ntem, the Mungo, the Cross River) |
| (iii) Capital of the North Region | **Garoua** |
| (iv) A man-made lake | **Lake Lagdo** (on the River Benoue, behind the Lagdo Dam); others: Lake Bamendjin (Noun river), Lake Mbakaou |
| (v) A game reserve | **The Dja Faunal Reserve** (others: the Douala-Edea Wildlife Reserve, the Kimbi Game Reserve) |
| (vi) A dam recently constructed | **The Lom Pangar dam** (East Region), or the **Memve'ele** dam on the Ntem (South Region); another: Mekin |

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Give **FOUR** reasons of food waste in Cameroon.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any four reasons, one mark each.

1. **Poor storage and preservation:** farmers have few silos, stores or refrigerators, so crops such as tomatoes, plantains, fruits and fish rot or are eaten by pests after harvest.
2. **Bad roads and poor transport:** food from remote villages takes long to reach the market, and it is damaged or spoiled on the way.
3. **Lack of food processing industries:** the surplus of the harvest season cannot be turned into flour, juice, canned or dried food, and much of it is thrown away.
4. **Poor marketing and overproduction in season:** there is no good market information, so many crops are left in the field when prices fall.
5. **Lack of electricity and cold chains,** pests and diseases, bad handling and packing, and wastage in homes, restaurants and hotels.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Describe **TWO** benefits of each of the following to the economy of Cameroon:

(i) The extraction of timber,
(ii) The completion of the construction of the Douala - Yaounde motorway,
(iii) The mining of bauxite,
(iv) Her membership in CEMAC,
(v) The construction of many HEP stations.

(10 marks)

(Total = 20 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two benefits for each item, one mark each (10 marks).

**(i) Extraction of timber**
1. It earns **foreign exchange**: timber is one of the main exports of Cameroon, and the State and local councils collect taxes and forest royalties.
2. It gives **jobs** in felling, sawmills, transport and ports, and supplies raw materials to the wood and furniture industries.

**(ii) Completion of the Douala - Yaounde motorway**
1. It **reduces the travel time and the accidents** between the two biggest cities, and relieves the congestion of the old national road.
2. It makes the **transport of goods easier and faster** from the port of Douala to Yaounde and to the neighbouring countries, which boosts trade and industry and gives jobs during construction.

**(iii) Mining of bauxite** (deposits at Minim-Martap and Ngaoundal in the Adamawa Region)
1. It earns **foreign exchange and government revenue** from the export of the ore or of alumina.
2. It provides **jobs** and encourages the building of railways and roads, and gives raw material for the aluminium industry (for example at Edea), which reduces imports.

**(iv) Membership in CEMAC** (Central African Economic and Monetary Community: Cameroon, Chad, the Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea)
1. It gives Cameroon a **bigger market** for its goods (food, manufactured goods) in the member states, with reduced customs barriers, and the port of Douala earns money from goods in transit to Chad and the Central African Republic.
2. It gives a **stable common currency** (the CFA franc), which makes trade and investment easier, and allows shared projects (roads, energy) financed by regional banks.

**(v) Construction of many HEP (hydroelectric power) stations**
1. It supplies **cheap and clean electricity** to homes, industries and towns, which encourages industries and reduces the need for imported fuel.
2. It creates **jobs** during construction and operation, and the dams also help with water supply, irrigation, fishing and flood control, and some power can be exported.
